d1911ccc39.why: Fact error fixed. Maize has separate male and female flowers, and Darwin's self-fertilised seed came from a single plant set apart and left to fertilise itself (darwin-online MS DAR65.86r), so 'a flower given pollen from its own plant' is true. The key, controlled variables, is the classification that the lead's ruling gives this unit. It is not a bare definition: the choices make the student tell held-the-same conditions apart from a control group and from the changed and measured variables. It does not re-key 9b05eb0ae2 (independent and dependent) or T1 206806948f (why keep things the same).

b54fe71bc3.why: The standout is fixed: all four choices now say what Sam did. 'Sprays' removes the soaking confound, so 'changed two things' is gone and nothing in the stem rules out a lure. The key (one seed a group) sits inside a described design with chance at work, which is the lead's stated exception, so it is not T1 d206b22021's repeat or T2 cba5994641's fluke run. It is true: some seeds are dead or dormant (Grokipedia, Germination), and the Darwin quote is documented. The lures are on the weak side (same packet, indoors) but stay wrong and plausible to a 7th grader.

d0930f8ddf.why: The dates are fixed. 'Around 1890' matches Britannica, which dates the chickens' illness to 1890, and Grokipedia, which has the colonies from 1889. 'Through the early 1890s' fits Eijkman's leaving Java in 1896, and the Grokipedia-only chicken count is cut. Key and lures are unchanged and sound (a matched control, against no control, cure-only and a confounded place). Thiamine and the 1929 Nobel are true. No other final uses Eijkman, and the question keys none of Lind, blinding or placebos.

68158e1640.why: Re-asks T1 measuring-and-the-fair-test e1be3638ed in a new scene. That question's key is to accept results that go against the idea ('Change his idea to fit the results'), and its lures are this question's three lures in other words: 'Call the whole test a failure' is 'Nothing, as the test found no difference'; 'Decide the big magnet must be broken' is 'The class must have made a mistake somewhere'; 'Keep his idea, but leave out these results' is 'The wax helps, but something hid its effect'. T2 caeaf20e1e's lure 'His results tell nothing about it yet' adds the same 'shows nothing' trap. A student who learned the T1 lesson answers this with no 7th-grade knowledge, and the 'no difference' twist adds no new misconception. The key also nearly restates the stem's result ('slide just as far' becomes 'did not help'). The facts themselves are true (Wikipedia, Null result). No one-phrase fix: re-aim it at a design point this unit does not yet key, or drop it.
